series.provider: Central Bank of the United Arab Emirates
series.definition_note: Three-month Emirates Interbank Offered Rate (EIBOR) fixing, percent a year, administered by the Central Bank of the United Arab Emirates and published on its EIBOR Rates page. EIBOR is the daily reference rate at which panel banks are able and willing to obtain UAE dirham funding in reasonable market size (AED 10 million or more) from the UAE money market just before 11:00 UAE time. The calculation agent (Refinitiv) fixes it each UAE business day as the mean of the panel submissions left after the top and bottom quartiles are trimmed wherever possible, and publishes it at 12:00 UAE time to five decimal places (CBUAE EIBOR regulations, effective 15 April 2018, amended 6 May 2020 and 1 January 2022, Annex II and Schedule 2). One value per fixing date: not averaged, not adjusted, and the later value date is not used. Read from the EIBOR chart data behind the CBUAE home page (JSON element eibor-home-chart-data, array historicalThreeMonth), which reaches back to June 2018 with most days of 2018 and January 2019 missing. Days without a fixing are absent.

Registered with ``calculated_by`` "OECD" because the dataflow applies the OECD's own transformation dimension to a level series; INDEC states the identical concept (series desestacionalizada, variación respecto al trimestre anterior) in its own quarterly report and workbook, and this route's values agree with INDEC's own workbook to eight or nine significant figures (not merely after rounding: -0.591773011 here against INDEC's -0.5917730153881138 for 2026-Q2), but INDEC publishes no keyless, stable-URL machine-readable route of its own for this figure (INDEC renames the workbook with each release, and the Ministry of Economy's mirror carries only the GDP level, not this growth rate). This is not annualised: it is the rate The Daily's opening paragraph and Table 2 ('Real gross domestic product by expenditure account, quarterly change') state, for example 'Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased 0.8% in the second quarter of 2026' (The Daily, 28 August 2026). StatCan labels this table's seasonal adjustment 'Seasonally adjusted at annual rates', naming how the underlying dollar levels are scaled, not this growth rate; the rate itself is not compounded to an annual rate. StatCan revises earlier quarters with each release as new and revised source data arrive.

Statistics Canada, Gross domestic product, expenditure-based, Canada, quarterly (table 36-10-0104-01, formerly CANSIM 380-0064): real gross domestic product at market prices, chained (2017) dollars, quarter-on-quarter percentage change at an annual rate, seasonally adjusted, quarterly, percent, as the Web Data Service states it (vector v79448580, coordinate 1.4.1.30, 'Contributions to percent change, annualized', three decimals; for the total itself this equals its own annualised change). This is the rate The Daily's Table 3 ('Real gross domestic product by expenditure account, annualized change') states, for example 3.3% (3.316 to three decimals) for the second quarter of 2026, StatCan's own annualisation of the same release's quarter-on-quarter rate (0.8% that quarter); it is StatCan's stated figure, never derived here from the non-annualised rate. StatCan revises earlier quarters with each release as new and revised source data arrive.

series.dataset: SNB data portal cube plkopr (Consumer prices – total)
series.definition_note: Swiss Consumer Price Index (Landesindex der Konsumentenpreise), all items, compiled and published monthly by the Swiss Federal Statistical Office (FSO). Change from the same month of the previous year in percent: the month's index against the same month a year earlier, not an annual average; not seasonally adjusted. Taken from the Swiss National Bank data portal, cube plkopr (Consumer prices – total, source stated as the FSO), item VVP, series key EPB@SNB.plkopr{VVP}, stored unrounded as the portal's API gives it. The FSO states the rate to one decimal, and so does the portal's own table; the API's further digits are not a rate the FSO states: in every month from January 2023 to August 2026 the API value equals, to within 1e-14, the change between the FSO's published four-decimal index levels (December 2025 = 100) a year apart, so it is the change calculated from the FSO index (the portal does not say who calculates it). Rounded to one decimal, the values equal the FSO's published rates in all those months. The portal marks no series break over those months. The portal republishes each month about the 21st of the following month, some two and a half weeks after the FSO's release. This is the national CPI, not the harmonised index (HICP) that Eurostat publishes for Switzerland. Requested from January 2023.

series.dataset: FSO table je-d-03.03.01.03 (Erwerbslosenquote gemäss ILO nach Geschlecht, Nationalität und Altersgruppen, brutto- und saisonbereinigte Werte), sheet Quartalswerte
series.definition_note: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (FSO), Unemployment Statistics based on the ILO definition (Erwerbslosenstatistik gemäss ILO), derived from the Swiss Labour Force Survey (SLFS): the ILO unemployment rate, ILO unemployed as a percentage of the labour force, permanent resident population, quarterly average, seasonally adjusted, percent. Seasonal adjustment is X-12-ARIMA and is recalculated every quarter, so the whole adjusted series is revised with each release. The table's number format states one decimal and values are rounded to it, as published. The FSO's release title states the unadjusted rate against the same quarter a year earlier (4.9% for 2026-Q2); the adjusted rate is its quarter-on-quarter measure (5.0% to 5.1%). The table's unadjusted total equals the Swiss rate the FSO gives for ages 15-74 in its EU comparison. Break stated in the workbook's note: with the July 2024 release the FSO revised 2021-Q1 to 2024-Q1, removing implausible cases, reweighting and adding social assistance receipt to the post-stratification. This is not SECO's registered unemployment rate, a different and lower measure. The workbook states no release date.

Percent (OECD unit code PA), monthly, comparing the month's index with the same month a year earlier (no averaging), neither seasonally nor calendar adjusted, national coverage (the metadata names 500 rural and urban areas). Stored as the OECD gives it, not rounded; the NBS states one decimal, and a value with more rejects. Every observation carries the normal status. From January 2026 the NBS compiles the CPI on a 2025 base with a revised basket, outlets and weights; it estimates the effect on the 12-month changes at about 0.06 percentage points on average. The OECD flags no break. Requested from January 2023. The OECD is migrating countries to its COICOP 2018 dataflow (DSD_PRICES_COICOP2018@DF_PRICES_C2018_ALL); China was not in it on 27 September 2026. National consumer price index of households (IPC national, all items; the BCC's tables head it 'Décembre 2011 = 100'), 12-month change in percent (glissement annuel), produced by the Institut National de la Statistique and published by the Central Bank of the Congo on its statistics portal (dataset inflation, series inflation--glissement-annuel, monthly rows from January 2022). The INS measures the 12-month change weekly, against the corresponding week of the previous year; each monthly value is the reading for the month's last week (end of period), as the weekly rows of the same series and table II.4 of the BCC's Condensé hebdomadaire d'informations statistiques show. A month whose monthly value disagrees with its last weekly reading is stored as missing (June 2026: the monthly row repeats week III's 2.772; table II.4 gives 2.869 for week IV). No seasonal adjustment is stated. Rounded to the three decimals the series and table II.4 state; recent values are carried unrounded in the payload. No break is flagged; the published monthly change for October 2025 is -4.348% (12-month rate 7.792% in September 2025, 2.519% in October).

Official indicative exchange rate (cours indicatif) of the Central Bank of the Congo, Congolese francs per US dollar: the buying and selling rates of the central bank, licensed banks and bureaux de change, weighted by transaction volume. One value per business day from the BCC's reference history (dataset cours-de-change, series cours-de-change--usd-cdf), stored from 2025. Each rate is dated by the business day on which it applies, as the BCC's daily rates page dates it. The history matches table IV.1 (interbank rates, daily averages at opening) of the BCC's weekly Condensé hebdomadaire d'informations statistiques date for date, and table IV.3 lists the rate one business day earlier, on the day it is set. The history lags the daily rates page by one or more business days, and on a few dates (for example 19 February, 24 March and 28-29 April 2026) it differs from the rate that page gives; where checked (19 February, 28-29 April 2026) it agrees with table IV.1. The BCC publishes each rate ahead of the day it applies; a rate dated after the retrieval day is not stored. As quoted; not inverted. Rounded to the two decimals the series and table IV.1 state; the daily rates page and table IV.3 quote four decimals, and some days carry more digits in the payload. A dollar rate equal to the same day's euro rate rejects the payload (the history and table IV.1 repeat the euro rate as the dollar rate on 7 June 2023). No fixing time is stated.

Marginal rate, percent, at the Central Bank of the Congo's auction of 84-day (12-week) Bons BCC, the central bank bills with which it absorbs bank liquidity (dataset bons-bcc, series bons-bcc--taux-marginal-84-jours; the same rates appear by auction date in table V.3 of the BCC's Condensé hebdomadaire d'informations statistiques). It is the nearest official 3-month rate the BCC publishes; it is neither an interbank nor a Treasury bill rate. One value per auction date, usually weekly; the publisher labels the dataset daily. Stored from 2025: the 84-day tranche was offered only sporadically before it resumed on 26 November 2025, and the portal's row for 2 October 2024 reads 253 where table V.3 states 25.00. Auction dates without an 84-day tranche are not stored. A published 0 is stored as missing, not as a rate of zero: table V.3 prints 0.00 when the tranche has no allotment (22 July 2026: no bids). A rate above 100 percent rejects the payload. Rounded to the two decimals the series and table V.3 state.

series.definition_note: CAPMAS consumer price index for Urban Egypt, all items, 2018/2019 base: annual change rate in percent (change on the same month a year earlier), monthly. CAPMAS indicator 2264, filter 3443 'Urban Egypt', publication 32 'Consumer Price Index'. This is the rate CAPMAS's monthly CPI bulletin gives for Urban Egypt, All Items; the bulletin lists the Total Egypt rate first, which differs from it, and neither the Total Egypt nor the Rural Egypt rate is stored. No seasonal adjustment is stated. Values are stored as the API returns them: one decimal, except November 2020, which the API carries unrounded (5.696186046); the API states no precision, so nothing is rounded. The 2018/2019-base rates start in September 2019; the January 2010-base rates before them (indicator 1799) are a separate series and are not spliced on.

Egyptian pounds per US dollar (units), monthly average, as published by the International Monetary Fund in its Exchange Rates dataset (IMF.STA:ER, the successor of the IFS Exchange Rate Indicators), series EGY.XDC_USD.PA_RT.M: indicator XDC_USD 'Domestic currency per US Dollar', transformation PA_RT 'Period average', monthly. The IMF compiles the rate from the Central Bank of Egypt: its International Financial Statistics country notes describe Egypt's market rate as 'the rate quoted by the Central Bank of Egypt', and IFS defines the period average as the monthly average of the reporting country's market or official rates. The IMF marks each monthly average raw data (derivation type R), not an IMF staff calculation, but does not say whether the Central Bank of Egypt or the IMF averaged the daily rates; nothing is averaged here. Stored as the IMF quotes it, not inverted and not rounded (the payload states no precision). No seasonal adjustment; the payload states no break. The series runs about two months behind: on 27 September 2026 the latest month was July 2026. series.instrument: 10-year benchmark institutional Hong Kong SAR Government Bond (HKD, fixed rate), closing reference yield, monthly average
series.definition_note: Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Monthly Statistical Bulletin table 10.4.2.1 (workbook T10040201.xls, sheet 'T10.4.2.1 (Benchmark yields)', column N): yield of the 10-year benchmark institutional Hong Kong SAR Government Bond (Hong Kong dollar, fixed rate) issued under the Infrastructure Bond Programme and Government Sustainable Bond Programme, Closing Reference Pricings, percent per annum. Monthly (period) average of the daily closing reference yields, which Bloomberg calculates as the HKMA's calculating agent from primary dealers' quotes as at 4:00 pm Hong Kong time and rounds to three decimals; the workbook holds the unrounded average formatted to three decimals, and the value is rounded to that stated format, as the table and the HKMA's API show it. Not seasonally adjusted. The benchmark is a specific issue that the HKMA replaces from time to time, usually when a new 10-year issue is tendered. The table starts in October 2024; the 10-year tenor has no benchmark ('-') until December 2024, stored as missing, and the first 10-year average is January 2025. The earlier Government Bond Programme benchmark series (table 9.4.1) is not spliced on.

3-month Hong Kong dollar interbank offered rate fixing (HKD Interest Settlement Rate, HIBOR fixing), as the Hong Kong Monetary Authority republishes it in its Monthly Statistical Bulletin table 6.3.3 (workbook T060303.xls, sheet 'T6.3.3 (HIBOR Fixing)', column G), percent per annum, five decimals, one fixing per business day as at 11:15 am Hong Kong time; a daily fixing, not a period average, and not seasonally adjusted. An interbank offered rate, not a Treasury bill rate. The Hong Kong Association of Banks is the source and owner of the fixing: the average of the middle quotes of the 12-20 reference banks it designates, after the three highest and three lowest are excluded. The HKMA refreshes the table monthly, so the latest day is usually the previous month-end. 'N.A.' is stored as missing. Days from 1 January 2023 are read.

Calculated by the International Monetary Fund: IMF Consumer Price Index dataset (IMF.STA:CPI(5.0.0)), series IRN.CPI._T.YOY_PCH_PA_PT.M. Whose index: the IMF's index (IRN.CPI._T.IX.M) is the consumer price index of the Statistical Centre of Iran (SCI) for all households of the country, urban and rural, 1400=100. The IMF restates it to the one decimal SCI publishes and files each Iranian month under the Gregorian month in which it ends (Tir 1405, 22 June to 22 July 2026, as 2026-07). The IMF's calculation: on 28 September 2026 every month equalled that index over the index a year earlier, minus one, times 100, to within 3e-14, carried to full floating-point precision; the IMF marks the rows 'reported official data'. SCI states its own rate to one decimal; from May 2023 to September 2025 the two agreed to within 0.13 points. Latest month on 28 September 2026: July 2026 (Tir 1405) = 87.92. For that month SCI's release of 29 July 2026 states the index as 676.9 and the point-to-point change as 87.9. Discrepancy with the Central Bank of Iran (CBI): the CBI compiles a separate index for urban areas only (1400=100). Its point-to-point change for Tir 1405 was 83.9 (index 742.8), 4.0 points below the IMF's figure. From September 2025 to July 2026 the IMF's figure exceeded the CBI's by 1.3 to 9.7 points. Headlines: the rate the CBI headlines as its inflation rate is the change in the average index of the last 12 months on the 12 months before (61.4 for Tir 1405), a different concept. SCI states the index with its monthly, point-to-point and 12-month-average changes together (3.1, 87.9 and 66.0 for Tir 1405), and calls only the 12-month average the annual inflation rate. Comparability: the other economies' figures are the change of the all-items index on the same month a year earlier. SCI's point-to-point change and the IMF's figure are that concept for the whole country, and SCI states that the law makes it responsible for price index statistics; the CBI's point-to-point change is that concept for urban areas only. Before May 2022 the IMF's index is an earlier series linked to SCI's, so months before May 2023 are not requested. Not rounded: the payload states no precision. Lag: SCI released Mordad 1405 (2026-08; point-to-point 89.0) on 27 August 2026, while on 28 September 2026 the IMF's latest month was July 2026, so the IMF trails SCI by about one month. A latest month with a value more than three months before the retrieval month rejects.

The rate is DOSM's own, not derived here from the index. Requested from January 2022.

MYR per US dollar, daily average of observations, compiled by the BIS (WS_XRU) from central bank and other official data, as quoted by the BIS; not inverted. The last 100 daily observations are requested.

Overnight policy rate, percent, compiled by the BIS from central bank data (WS_CBPOL, daily, end of period), from January 2020 and reduced to the days each level changed; the first day is a starting level. The BIS compilation note must name the "overnight policy rate". Dates are those of the BIS daily series.

Unemployment rate from DOSM's monthly Labour Force Survey: unemployed persons as a percentage of the labour force, persons aged 15 to 64 (the survey's working age), seasonally adjusted (catalogue lfs_month_sa, column u_rate, the same figures as Table B of the monthly Labour Force release), one decimal as published. Break: DOSM's July 2026 release estimates figures to December 2023 on 2010 Census population data and figures from January 2024 on 2020 Census data, while the catalogue's caveat places the switch at 2025. The release also states that some 2025 months were revised to the latest population estimates and that 2026 figures use population projections. Requested from January 2022.

Headline (all items) composite consumer price index, percentage change from the same month of the previous year, produced by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) and republished by the Central Bank of Nigeria in its Inflation table (column 'All Items (Year on Change)', field allItemsYearOn), monthly, percent, two decimals as published. Neither publisher states a seasonal adjustment. Break: from January 2025 the rates come from the NBS's rebased CPI (price reference 2024=100, weights 2023); the rates up to December 2024 are those the NBS published on its earlier CPI, base November 2009=100 (34.80 in December 2024, 27.61 in January 2025). The table carries the NBS's current figures, not first releases: the NBS first gave January 2025 at 24.48 (rebasing highlights, February 2025) and now gives 27.61. June 2025 is missing: the CBN's row for it repeats May 2025 in all eight values (26.06 headline), while the NBS states June 2025 at 25.29.

series.dataset: CBN Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market rates (api/GetAllNFEM_Rates)
series.definition_note: Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) rate, naira per US dollar, as the Central Bank of Nigeria quotes it (column 'NFEM Rate (₦/US$)', field weightedAvgRate); not inverted. The CBN states that the NFEM rate 'is derived at Volume Weighted Average and stands as the official exchange rate for the day'. One value per business day from 2 December 2024, when the table starts; four decimals as published. No fixing time is stated. A date the table lists twice with identical values is stored once.

series.dataset: CBN Government Securities, NTB primary market (api/GetAllSecuritiesNTB)
series.instrument: Nigerian Treasury Bill, 91-day, primary auction marginal rate
series.definition_note: Marginal (stop) rate, percent, at the Central Bank of Nigeria's primary-market auctions of 91-day Nigerian Treasury Bills (field rate, which the Government Securities Summary labels 'Marginal Rate'), one value per auction date, usually every one or two weeks; four decimals as published. The CBN does not state whether the rate is a discount rate or a yield; its separate 'True Yield' field is 0.0000 for all but one 91-day auction since 2022 and is not read. It is a Treasury bill rate, not an interbank rate; the only interbank rate in the CBN's Money Market Indicators table is its monthly 'Inter-Bank Call Rate'. Tenor labels vary ('91DAY', '91 Day', '91 DAYS'); a '90 DAY' special auction is not included. Dated by the auction date the CBN states. Two auctions the CBN misdates are left out, not re-dated: the row dated 11 June 2024 (auction number '06-11-2024', maturing 6 February 2025) and the row dated 9 September 2025 (auction number '03-09-2025', maturing 4 December 2025). The rate rose from 5.00 at the auction of 24 January 2024 to 17.24 at the auction of 7 February 2024, a move in the market rate that the table does not mark as a break.

Break: from the January 2026 index SSB classifies consumption by ECOICOP version 2 (derived from COICOP 2018) and references the index to 2025=100, and it recalculated earlier indices on the new classification. The rates for months before 2026 in this table come from that recalculated series, and SSB says they may differ from the rates it published before 2026, mainly from rounding; when this series was registered, 15 of the 36 months of 2023-2025 differed by 0.1 point from the closed table 03013 (for example January 2024: 4.8 here against 4.7 in table 03013, as published at the time). The figures come from the 'Total' row of the table beside the chart 'Unemployment rate by sex, seasonally adjusted' on Stats NZ's unemployment rate indicator page, which ran from the June 2012 quarter when this route was registered. The release date is the date the page states it was updated, which must fall after the quarter ends.

series.definition_note: Consumer price inflation for Russia: percent change on the same month of the previous year (column "Инфляция, % г/г"), monthly, a 12-month change of unadjusted consumer prices. Published by the Bank of Russia in its database table "Инфляция и ключевая ставка Банка России", which names Rosstat and the Bank of Russia as sources. Read from the table's own XLSX export (query 132934, column C) from January 2022 and stored to the two decimals stated. The table's key rate column (the rate on the last day of each month) and its 4% target column are not stored.

series.dataset: Bank of Russia database: Russian Government Bond Zero Coupon Yield Curve
series.definition_note: Bank of Russia database table "Russian Government Bond Zero Coupon Yield Curve" (Russian page: "Кривая бескупонной доходности государственных облигаций"), percent per annum, one value per trading day, column "10" of remaining maturity in years. The Russian page refers readers to PJSC Moscow Exchange for details of the curve, the zero-coupon yield curve (G-curve) the Exchange fits to OFZ federal loan bonds. This is the curve's 10-year point: a fitted zero-coupon yield, not the yield to maturity of one benchmark bond, stated to two decimals. Rows start on 1 June 2026; a dash stays missing.

Key rate, percent, compiled by the BIS from central bank data (WS_CBPOL, daily, end of period), from January 2020 and reduced to the days each level changed; the first day is a starting level. The BIS compilation note must name the "key rate". Dates are those of the BIS daily series.

Unemployment rate of the Russian Federation, percent of the labour force, ILO definition, persons aged 15 and older, not seasonally adjusted, monthly, calculated by the International Monetary Fund: IMF Labor Statistics dataset (IMF.STA:LS(9.0.0)), series RUS.U.PT.M 'Unemployment rate, Percent'. The IMF calculates it as unemployed persons over the labour force from the unrounded Labour Force Survey estimates of the Federal State Statistics Service (Rosstat) it holds (series RUS.UP.PE.M and RUS.LF.PE.M, the labour force being employed plus unemployed persons): on 27 September 2026 every month from January 2023 equalled that ratio times 100 to within 1e-13, carried to full floating-point precision (2026-06 = 2.22547648152004), whereas Rosstat states the rate to one decimal; the IMF marks the rows 'reported official data'. Age scope, adjustment and coverage as Rosstat states them in its SDDS metadata on the IMF's Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board: survey of private households, persons aged 15 and older, no seasonal adjustment of the monthly results, all regions except the Donetsk and Lugansk 'people's republics' and the Zaporozhye and Kherson regions; in 2023-2024 Rosstat recalculated its 2013-2022 results on the 2020 census, before the requested range. Not rounded: the payload states no precision. The metadata give Rosstat's timeliness as the 30th to 34th business day after the month; on 27 September 2026 the IMF's latest month was June 2026, while Rosstat's July figure had been released on 2 September 2026, so the IMF trails Rosstat by about one month. Requested from January 2023; a latest month with a value more than three months before the retrieval month rejects.

The average of the closing bid rates that SGS primary dealers quote to each other for standard market lots (the average buying rates of government securities dealers); prices quoted to others may differ. series.instrument: 12-week MAS Bill (Monetary Authority of Singapore bill), daily closing bid yield
series.definition_note: Monetary Authority of Singapore, MAS Bills Historical Prices - Benchmark Issues: yield of the 12-week MAS Bill, percent per annum, daily. MAS Bills are zero-coupon bills issued at a discount by MAS in its money market operations to manage banking system liquidity, with tenors of 4, 12 or 36 weeks; the 12-week bill (84 days) is the tenor nearest three months. The average of the closing bid rates that primary dealers quote to each other for standard market lots; one closing value per business day, not a monthly average. It is a central bank bill rate, not an interbank or Treasury bill rate: MAS discontinued its 3-month interbank rate from 1 January 2014 and issued the final 3-month SGS T-bill on 20 June 2013. Read from the MAS statistics API that serves the MAS Bills Statistics page (product type M, field bid_12w_mbill_yield); the latest 90 business days are requested.

Break in January 2026: from that month the index is on the 2025=100 base named in the table heading, with a changed consumption basket classification and updated weights (CBRT, January 2026 Price Developments). Türkiye's real gross domestic product, chain-linked volumes, percentage change on the previous quarter, seasonally and calendar adjusted, published by Eurostat in namq_10_gdp (unit CLV_PCH_PRE, s_adj SCA, na_item B1GQ, geo TR). Eurostat's metadata for this dataset states that Eurostat estimates only the EU and euro-area aggregates and that all other rows, including candidate countries such as Türkiye, are produced by the respective country's own statistical office: this is the Turkish Statistical Institute's (TURKSTAT) own quarter-on-quarter GDP growth rate, republished unchanged, not a Eurostat calculation. TURKSTAT's own data portal could not be read directly by this collector (a JavaScript single-page application whose API answers 403 Access denied and whose SDMX service answers 401 Unauthorized), so this route is used instead. Checked 29 September 2026: the latest value, 2026-Q2 = 1.1, matches TURKSTAT's press release of 31 August 2026 ("Gross Domestic Product, Quarter II: April-June, 2026"), which stated GDP grew 1.1% on the previous quarter on a seasonally and calendar adjusted basis, as carried the same day by independent reporting of that release. Requested from 2015-Q1 and stored as Eurostat publishes it, to one decimal.

Türkiye's unemployment rate, persons aged 15 and over, seasonally adjusted, percent of the labour force, monthly, published by Eurostat in une_rt_m (unit PC_ACT, sex T, age TOTAL, s_adj SA, geo TR). The data are TURKSTAT's Household Labour Force Survey estimates: Eurostat's metadata lists Turkey among the countries whose monthly estimates come directly from the Labour Force Survey and whose seasonally adjusted series is delivered with the unadjusted one, so Eurostat does not model or seasonally adjust them, and it says Eurostat calculates each country's rate from the delivered levels of unemployed and employed persons. The same metadata says Turkey's 25-74 age group is to be read as 25 and over under the national methodology, so age TOTAL here covers ages 15 and over, not the 15 to 74 of Eurostat's general definition. The result is TURKSTAT's own headline: checked on 27 September 2026, every month from January 2023 to July 2026 equalled, at the one decimal both show, TURKSTAT's revised table "Seasonally adjusted main labour force indicators (15+ age)" released with Labour Force Statistics, July 2026 on 31 August 2026 (July 8.1, June 7.6). TURKSTAT publishes first and revises earlier seasonally adjusted months with each release, and Eurostat takes them up later: on 27 September 2026 Eurostat's latest month was July, and TURKSTAT's August figure was due on 30 September 2026. Eurostat flags breaks in January 2007 and January 2014, before the requested window; none is flagged from January 2023. Requested from January 2023 and stored as Eurostat publishes it, to one decimal.

Read from the monthly series "CPI Change Rate (yoy, %)" in the chart data of DGBAS's Latest Indicators page; the annual series on the same page, which carries a forecast for the current year, is not used. The CPI is a Laspeyres index covering the whole territory; DGBAS rebases it periodically and publishes the year-on-year rate itself, so nothing is computed from the index here. DGBAS revises the CPI for up to three months after first publication, and the page carries the revised figures, not the first release. Kept from January 2022.

table_gaps.reason: Ukraine's State Statistics Service has not published its Labour Force Survey unemployment rate since the fourth quarter of 2021.
Ukraine has no 10-year government bond benchmark, and the National Bank publishes no such yield.
The National Bank discontinued its UIIR interbank index in 2020; its successor, UONIA, is an overnight rate.
The Democratic Republic of the Congo has no 10-year government bond market.

The Institut National de la Statistique publishes no unemployment series: its statistics cover debt, investment, inflation, mining, poverty and GDP, and labour figures appear only in one-off survey reports (checked 28 September 2026).
No official body publishes a 10-year government bond yield for Argentina; quoted yields are exchange prices.
The Central Bank publishes no 3-month interbank, deposit or bill rate; its BADLAR and TAMAR rates are 30 to 35-day deposit rates.
Iran issues no 10-year government bond; its Islamic government securities run one to three years.
No 3-month money-market, interbank or Treasury bill rate is published; the interbank market rate states no maturity.

table_gaps.short_reason: No rate named as the policy rate
table_gaps.reason: The Central Bank of Iran lists its interbank rate, repo cut-off rate and corridor rates, but names none of them as its policy rate.
Only the Central Bank's Economic Trends bulletin reproduces the rate, one quarter per issue, and the Statistical Centre of Iran's site could not be reached (checked 28 September 2026).

table_gaps.short_reason: Not published by an official body
table_gaps.reason: Neither the State Bank of Vietnam nor the statistics office publishes a 10-year yield; the Hanoi Stock Exchange's yield curve is an exchange's, not an official statistic.
No official 10-year benchmark yield series was found for Saudi Arabia; the DataSaudi portal carries no yields.
No official yield series was found; the Qatar Central Bank's notices state the bids received at bond auctions, not yields.

table_gaps.short_reason: QIBOR: the central bank's terms forbid republishing
table_gaps.reason: The 3-month QIBOR fixing is collected from the Qatar Central Bank, whose terms do not allow it to be republished, so it is kept off this site.
Qatar's open-data portal holds only annual unemployment rates to 2023 and quarterly labour-force counts.
The Federal Competitiveness and Statistics Centre's data portal refuses automated access (HTTP 403, checked 28 September 2026).

The Federal Competitiveness and Statistics Centre's data portal refuses automated access (HTTP 403, checked 28 September 2026); its open-data files hold only annual rates ending between 2017 and 2021.

table_gaps.short_reason: Central bank site behind a bot challenge
table_gaps.reason: The Central Bank of the UAE's rate pages sit behind a bot challenge (HTTP 403, checked 28 September 2026), and the BIS compiles no UAE policy rate.
No official 10-year yield series was found for the UAE.
Egypt's Ministry of Finance lists no fixed-rate 10-year bond; its 10-year line is a floating-rate note.

table_gaps.short_reason: Central bank site rejects automated access
table_gaps.reason: The Central Bank of Egypt's site rejects automated access on every page (checked 28 September 2026), and the BIS compiles no Egyptian policy rate.
No current official 3-month money-market series was found; Brazil's CDI and Selic rates are overnight rates.
The Central Reserve Bank's statistics carry no 3-month interbank or Treasury bill rate.
The Bank of Russia's 31 to 90-day interbank rates are blank, its 3-month RUONIA average compounds past overnight rates, and its yield curve's shortest point is extrapolated.

table_gaps.short_reason: Debt office site refuses automated access
table_gaps.reason: The Debt Management Office's site refuses automated access (HTTP 403, checked 28 September 2026), and the Central Bank no longer publishes its bond table.
The National Bureau of Statistics publishes the Labour Force Survey only as PDF reports; the latest covers the second quarter of 2024.

table_gaps.short_reason: Central bank's EVDS data service requires a key
table_gaps.reason: The Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye publishes this yield only through its EVDS data service, which requires a registered key; registering one is planned.

table_gaps.short_reason: Statistics Indonesia's data service requires a key
table_gaps.reason: Statistics Indonesia's site blocks automated access and its data service requires a registered key; registering one is planned. It publishes the rate twice a year.

The National Bureau of Statistics states the surveyed urban unemployment rate in its monthly release (5.3% in August 2026), but its site cannot be reached from our data collection (checked 28 and 29 September 2026).
Liechtenstein's central government has no debt outstanding, so there is no government bond yield (S&P Global Ratings' report of 25 November 2024, published by the government).

table_gaps.short_reason: Stated only in daily operation notices
table_gaps.reason: The People's Bank of China states its policy rate, the 7-day reverse repo rate (1.40% on 28 September 2026), only in daily open-market operation notices, not as a series or a decision release; the BIS compiles its 1-year loan prime rate instead.

table_gaps.short_reason: Statistics office uses an untrusted certificate
table_gaps.reason: Rosstat's site uses a certificate chained to the Russian Trusted Root CA, which our data collection does not trust, and its EMISS portal refuses automated access.
